title: Walking Pace Calculator: Minutes per Mile and km
description: Convert a walk's distance and time into pace and speed with the Walking Pace Calculator — min per mile, min per km, mph and km/h. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 5 km in 50 minutes is a 10:00/km pace — 6.0 km/h, the brisk purposeful walk most health advice is secretly describing.
quick_answer: The Walking Pace Calculator converts a walk's distance and duration into pace — minutes per mile and per kilometre — and average speed. Enter how far you walked and how long it took and read the figures that turn one walk into the planning basis for every walk after it.

faq: Does this replace a specialist tool or professional measurement?
No — it is exact division of distance by time. GPS watches add splits and elevation; this is the arithmetic they must agree with.
Is my input uploaded?
No. The pace is computed in your browser.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Crossings and crowds are already inside the time you measured.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Enter the distance you actually walked — paths wind, and pace belongs to the real ground.
Can route results change over time?
Your pace will, with fitness and habit. Remeasure each season and plan with the current walker.
How is this different from the Hiking Pace Calculator?
Audience: this page is pavement-and-park walking; the hiking one is trails and hills, where Naismith's climb allowance enters. The division is the same citizen.
Moving or elapsed time?
Elapsed for planning arrivals, moving for judging fitness. The difference is your stops, quantified.
Pace on a treadmill versus outdoors?
Belts flatter: no wind, no crossings, perfect surface. Outdoor measurements are the planning-grade ones.
How many walks should I average?
Three typical walks steady the figure. One heroic outlier is a story, not a pace.
Pace worsens late in long walks.
Fatigue is a pace curve, not a pace. For long days, plan with your hour-three figure, not your hour-one.
